rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bodies share corporeality across their divisions, while each body's contingent size, position, shape, and qualities require an eternal creator to specify them.
rows.anchor: الأجسام متساوية في الجسمية لأنه يصح تقسيم الجسم إلى الفلكي والعنصري والكثيف واللطيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the equator, the celestial equator bisects daily circles; night and day do not differ for stars, every non-polar point rises and sets, and the ecliptic and Sun pass overhead twice yearly.
rows.anchor: لم يختلف هناك ليل كوكب مع نهاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At northern and southern latitudes the pole elevation changes, daily paths are divided unequally, and seasonal day and night lengths reverse between hemispheres; some stars become permanently visible or hidden.
rows.anchor: فأما سائر المدارات فيقطعها بقسمين مختلفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When pole elevation equals the ecliptic's greatest obliquity, the ecliptic passes overhead, but the Sun does so only at the summer solstice.
rows.anchor: وههنا يبطل طلوع قطبي فلك البروج وغروبهما إلا أنهما يماسان الأفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At still higher latitude neither the ecliptic nor Sun passes overhead, and the ecliptic's northern pole is always visible while its southern pole is always hidden.
rows.anchor: ويصير القطب الشمالي من فلك البروج أبدي الظهور ، والآخر أبدي الخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When pole elevation equals the complementary obliquity, the solstitial points only touch the horizon; the ecliptic aligns with it and day or night disappears at the respective solstice.
rows.anchor: وينعدم الليل هناك في الانقلاب الصيفي ، والنهار في الشتوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond that latitude, portions around the summer solstice stay visible and those around the winter solstice stay hidden; reversed zodiacal risings and settings can occur.
rows.anchor: يصير قوس من فلك البروج أبدي الظهور مما يلي المنقلب الصيفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the pole the celestial equator lies on the horizon, rising and setting cease, and half the year is day and half night.
rows.anchor: فيكون هناك معدل النهار منطبقا على الأفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The equator divides Earth into northern and southern halves; the inhabited land is said to occupy one northern quarter, while three quarters are said to be water, with the caveat God knows best.
rows.anchor: والذي وجد معمورا من الأرض أحد الربعين الشماليين مع ما فيه من الجبال والبحار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabited world's length is nearly half the Earth's circumference by common agreement, but scholars disagree whether its western starting point is the encircling ocean coast or the Fortunate Islands.
rows.anchor: وجد طول العمارة قريبا من نصف الدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most place the inhabited breadth no farther than 66 degrees north; Ptolemy also posits habitation 16 degrees south, yielding about 82 degrees total.
rows.anchor: ولم يوجد عرض العمارة إلا إلى بعد ست وستين درجة من خط الإستواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Geographers divide inhabited land into seven longitudinal climates, starting at the equator or around 13 degrees north and ending near 50 degrees, beyond which settlement is sparse.
rows.anchor: ثم قسموا هذا القدر المعمور سبع قطع مستطيلة على موازاة خط الإستواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's varied terrain—land and sea, plains and mountains, rock and sand, hollows and heights—produces sharply differing conditions; he previously treated it under 2:22.
rows.anchor: كون بعضها بريا وبحريا ، وسهليا وجبليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is convex in longitude: a flat surface would experience simultaneous sunrise and sunset, contrary to differing eclipse times and elapsed night in eastern and western towns; a concave surface predicts the opposite time relation.
rows.anchor: ولما بطل القسمان ثبت أن طول الأرض محدب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lenticular rather than spherical longitudinal shape is rejected because eclipse durations vary across locations around a circle; thus Earth is spherical in longitude.
rows.anchor: فثبت أنها كرة في الطول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A flat or concave latitudinal surface conflicts with the changing pole altitude and visibility of circumpolar stars as a traveler moves south; Razi calls this persuasive reasoning.
rows.anchor: وهذه الحجة على حسن تقريرها إقناعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lunar eclipse is Earth's shadow; since the eclipsed portion is circular and the shadow follows the light-dark boundary, Earth is round from every side.
rows.anchor: وانخساف القمر مستدير لأنا نحس بالمقدار المنخسف منه مستديرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because all parts of Earth seek distance from the celestial sphere in the same way, Razi argues that Earth must be spherical.
rows.anchor: أن الأرض طالبة للبعد من الفلك ومتى كان حال جميع أجزائها كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics object that a centered spherical Earth should be surrounded by water seeking the center, and that its mountains and deep hollows contradict roundness.
rows.anchor: أن الماء محيطا بها من كل الجوانب ، لأن طبيعة الماء تقتضي طلب المركز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water objection is answered by divine providence exposing land like an island, or water flowing into low places and leaving some ground uncovered.
rows.anchor: العناية الإلهية اقتضت إخراج جانب من الأرض عن الماء بمنزلة جزيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountains and hollows are too small relative to Earth to overturn its spherical form, as small irregularities do not stop a wooden ball remaining round.
rows.anchor: هذه التضاريس لا تخرج الأرض عن كونها كرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's conditions more readily prove a creator than the heavens: terrestrial bodies visibly change their places and qualities, so their contingent specification requires an eternal, knowing director.
rows.anchor: الاستدلال بأحوال الأرض على وجود الصانع أسهل من الاستدلال بأحوال السموات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says the first reported interpretation of night-day difference is their succession, each replacing the one that has gone.
rows.anchor: اختلاف الليل والنهار تعاقبهما في الذهاب والمجيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reported interpretation is variation in night and day length, light and darkness, and increase and decrease.
rows.anchor: أراد اختلاف الليل والنهار في الطول والقصر والنور والظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi adds a third meaning: night and day also differ by location, so one instant is dawn in one longitude, noon elsewhere, and evening or night elsewhere; latitude changes seasonal lengths too.
rows.anchor: وعندي فيه وجه ثالث ، وهو أن الليل والنهار كما يختلفان بالطول والقصر في الأزمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night-day conditions point to a creator through eight signs: solar motion, seasons, daily work and rest, mutual benefit despite opposition, sleep and waking as a reminder of resurrection, dawn's advance through darkness, habitable moderate durations, and the Sun's special light-producing role.
rows.anchor: إن اختلاف أحوال الليل والنهار يدل على الصانع من وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gradual dawn breaking through darkness resembles a clear stream running through a turbid sea without either clouding the other; he links this image to the Quranic description of God splitting dawn.
rows.anchor: انشقاق ظلمة الليل بظهور الصبح المستطيل فيه من الآيات العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A temperate allocation of night and day permits life; near the pole, six months each of day and night would prevent ripening, habitation, and livelihood.
rows.anchor: تقدير الليل والنهار بالمقدار المعتدل الموافق للمصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God creates air-light at sunrise by habit, that needs no further argument; if the Sun itself causes it, the Sun's unique efficacy among equal bodies proves a maker.
rows.anchor: اختصاص الشمس بهذه الخاصية دون سائر الأجسام مع كون الأجسام بأسرها متماثلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that a huge powerful angel could move the heavens fails for Razi because human capacity cannot originate acts of creation.
rows.anchor: لما دل الدليل على أن قدرة العبد غير صالحة للإيجاد

rows.speaker: أبو هاشم
rows.claim: On the Mu'tazilite position, Abu Hashim dismisses the possibility that an angel moves the heavens by transmitted evidence.
rows.anchor: وأما على قول المعتزلة فقد نفى أبو هاشم هذا الاحتمال بالسمع

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi derives falak from rotation: it can mean anything round, the seven heavens' orbits, a girl's rounded breast, a spindle whorl, or a ship that turns easily on water.
rows.anchor: الفلك أصله من الدوران وكل مستدير فلك

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says falak is masculine when singular and feminine when plural; its matching written vowel differs in grammatical meaning, as in his examples for singular and plural nouns.
rows.anchor: الفلك إذا أريد به الواحد فضمة الفاء فيه بمنزلة ضمة باء برد

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says the sea is named for its vast breadth, and the verb can describe becoming extensive in knowledge or wealth.
rows.anchor: سمي البحر بحرا لاستبحاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another etymology derives sea from a split or incision in the earth, the same root as bahira.
rows.anchor: سمي البحر بحرا لأنه شق في الأرض والبحر الشق ومنه البحيرة

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i and other authorities on seas enumerate five major seas: Indian, Maghrib, Rum, Nitas, and Jurjan.
rows.anchor: أن البحور المعروفة خمسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Indian Ocean extends from the Ethiopian coast toward India and China, with four named gulfs, measured lengths and widths, and the Arabian lands between the Gulf of Aqaba and Persian Gulf.
rows.anchor: فإنه يمتد طوله من المغرب إلى المشرق ، من أقصى أرض الحبشة إلى أقصى أرض الهند والصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account lists 1,370 inhabited or uninhabited Indian Ocean islands; Serendib is large, mountainous, river-rich, and produces red ruby, while other islands supply tin and camphor.
rows.anchor: ألف وثلثمائة وسبعون جزيرة منها جزيرة ضخمة في أقصى البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Maghrib Ocean connects with the Indian Ocean; its far limits are unknown except to the west and north, ships sail near shore, and its account names the Fortunate Islands and a northern gulf toward Bulgaria.
rows.anchor: وهذا البحر لا تجري فيه السفن وإنما تسلك بالقرب من سواحله وفيه ست جزائر مقابل أرض الحبشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account gives lengths, widths, gulfs, and island counts for the Mediterranean, the Nitas/Black Sea, and the Jurjan/Caspian Sea; Jurjan does not connect to another sea.
rows.anchor: وأما بحر جرجان فطوله من المغرب إلى المشرق ثلثمائة ميل ، وعرضه ستمائة ميل

rows.speaker: أرسطاطاليس
rows.claim: Aristotle is cited as saying the Ocean surrounds Earth like a belt.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن أرسطاطاليس : أن بحر أوقيانوس ميحط بالأرض بمنزلة المنطقة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships depend on God-given materials and tools for construction, and on suitable winds for movement and safety; human beings cannot create or reverse the wind.
rows.anchor: لولا الرياح المعينة على تحريكها لما تكامل النفع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strengthens sailors' hearts to complete voyages and makes ships a means of livelihood, trade, and benefit to both shippers and recipients.
rows.anchor: لولا تقوية قلوب من يركب هذه السفن لما تم الغرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God apportions different goods among world regions and makes each region need others, prompting people to undertake dangerous voyages for mutual gain.
rows.anchor: خص كل طرف من أطراف العالم بشيء معين ، وأحوج الكل إلى الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sea is subdued to carry ships even though its power becomes frightening when storms and winds churn it.
rows.anchor: تسخير الله البحر لحمل الفلك مع قوة سلطان البحر إذا هاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Great rivers continually empty into the small Khwarazm lake without increasing or overflowing it, a water balance whose mechanism God knows.
rows.anchor: تنصب أبدا إلى بحيرة خوارزم على صغرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protects ships from the sea's immense animals and brings them safely to shore.
rows.anchor: ما في البحار من الحيوانات العظيمة ثم إن الله تعالى يخلص السفن عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The meeting of fresh and salt waters without mixing is another sign of God's governance, linked to two Quranic passages.
rows.anchor: بقدرته يحفظ البعض عن الاختلاط بالبعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that ships run for people's benefit implies permission to sail, earn through trade, and enjoy lawful pleasures.
rows.anchor: دل قوله على صفة الفلك : { بما ينفع الناس } على إباحة ركوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rainwater's substance and its thinness, moisture, and sweetness are God's creation; no one else can create it.
rows.anchor: من صفات الرقة ، والرطوبة ، والعذوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water gives humans life and many benefits, and is the basis of every living thing, as other verses state.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى جعله سببا لحياة الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rainwater also supplies livelihood, in keeping with the statement that provision is in heaven.
rows.anchor: كما جعله سببا لحياة الإنسان ، جعله سببا لرزقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds suspend immense quantities of water in the air, which he treats as a great sign.
rows.anchor: المياه العظيمة ، التي تسيل منها الأودية العظام تبقى معلقة في جو السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain arrives when creatures plead and need it, in a measured amount beneficial to them; he links this to Noah's call to seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: نزولها عند التضرع واحتياج الخلق إليه مقدرا بمقدار النفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses describe rain bringing life and growth to dead or barren land, reinforcing the sign.
rows.anchor: أنزلنا عليها الماء اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection asks whether rain descends literally from heaven, comes from clouds, or follows a natural account of evaporation and condensation.
rows.anchor: أفتقولون : إن الماء ينزل من السماء على الحقيقة أو من السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed natural account says the Sun heats Earth, vapors rise, cool and thicken, then join into raindrops.
rows.anchor: أن الشمس تؤثر في الأرض فيخرج منها أبخرة متصاعدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth's life after death includes vegetation that feeds livestock, crops that feed people, provision for animals, useful colors, tastes, scents, and materials for clothing, as well as the land's renewed beauty.
rows.anchor: ظهور النبات الذي هو الكلأ والعشب وما شاكلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling land alive or dead is metaphorical: only a perceiving, knowing subject literally lives or dies, while vegetation brings beauty, freshness, growth, and flourishing.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن وصفه تعالى ذلك بالإحياء بعد الموت مجاز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creator is evident in crops that no human can produce in their form, their countless colors and tastes, and their regular appearance at appointed times.
rows.anchor: أن إحياء الأرض بعد موتها يدل على الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi affirms that water descends from heaven as revelation says; if God can hold it in clouds, holding it in heaven is equally possible.
rows.anchor: قلنا : بل نقول إنه ينزل من السماء كما ذكره الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water from the seas on Earth is possible, but cannot be asserted decisively without denying a freely choosing creator and affirming an eternal world, which Razi calls unbelief.
rows.anchor: لكن القطع به لا يمكن إلا بعد القول بنفي الفاعل المختار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether animals arise by direct generation or by reproduction, their coming to be requires a wise maker; Razi begins by establishing this for humans.
rows.anchor: حدوث الحيوانات قد يكون بالتوليد ، وقد يكون بالتوالد

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In an anecdote, Umar says countless chess games on a small board rarely repeat, but the far greater variety of human faces on a face-sized area is more astonishing evidence of power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: فقال عمر بن الخطاب ههنا ما هو أعجب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A formative power in semen would need knowledge and skill beyond even the fully developed human, who cannot alter a single hair; an unconscious natural power would produce uniform effects, not a structured human.
rows.anchor: فثبت أنه لا بد للنطفة في انقلابها لحما ودما وإنسانا من مدبر ومقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The complex anatomy and arrangement of animal bodies provide further evidence, though their many marvels cannot be surveyed here.
rows.anchor: الاستدلال بأحوال تشريح أبدان الحيوانات والعجائب الواقعة في تركيبها وتأليفها

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali is reported to praise the One who gives sight through fat, hearing through bone, and speech through flesh.
rows.anchor: ما روى عن أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The body's elemental arrangement reverses the theorists' expected hierarchy: earth-like skull bone is uppermost, then water-like brain, air-like breath, and fire-like heart.
rows.anchor: عظم القحف والعظم بارد يابس على طبيعة الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human creation uniquely combines all four elements in ways other makers avoid, as the Quran describes Adam from earth, life from water, spirit from breath, and jinn from fire.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه وتعالى وضع نقش خلقته على هذه الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child cannot survive when its mouth and nose are blocked after birth, yet lives without breathing in the womb; its initially weak understanding later grows into the strongest animal intelligence, showing divine gift rather than nature.
rows.anchor: فإنك لو وضعت على فمه وأنفه ثوبا يقطع نفسه لمات في الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human languages, temperaments, constitutions, and appearances vary greatly, while wild and mountain animals resemble one another; human diversity preserves livelihood by preventing confusion of persons.
rows.anchor: اختلاف الألسنة واختلاف طبائعهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Air is created in a form that can be moved, then directed to benefit people, animals, and plants; its ubiquity reflects how vital it is, while rarer needs become progressively harder to obtain.
rows.anchor: مخلوقة على وجه يقبل التصريف

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet expresses that God makes scarce goods costly though people may do without them, and makes air easy to obtain although every breathing creature needs it.
rows.anchor: وعبر الشاعر عن هذا المعنى فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Winds drive ships, and no human or collection of humans can turn a north wind south or move still air at will.
rows.anchor: لولا تحرك الرياح لما جرت الفلك وذلك مما لا يقدر عليه أحد إلا الله

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi explains the syntax of wa-taṣrīf al-riyāḥ as an understood verbal noun with the object expressed by the genitive construction, a common usage.
rows.anchor: أراد وتصريفه الرياح فأضاف المصدر إلى المفعول وهو كثير

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says the singular rīḥ is a feminine form whose original wāw becomes yāʾ through the kasra; the few plural is arwāḥ, while the many plural riyāḥ has a kasra-driven change like dīma/diyam and ḥīla/ḥiyal.
rows.anchor: الريح اسم على فعل والعين منه واو انقلبت في الواحد للكسرة ياء

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: Ibn al-Anbari derives rīḥ from rūḥ because winds usually bring spirit and relief, whereas stillness brings distress; arwāḥ confirms the original wāw.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري : إنما سميت الريح ريحا لأن الغالب عليها في هبوبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four winds are north, south, eastward ṣabā, and westward dabūr; ṣabā is called qabūl because it faces dabūr, and intermediate directions are crosswinds.
rows.anchor: قالوا : الرياح أربع ، الشمال والجنوب

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr, Asim, and Ibn Amir read the word in the plural in ten locations, including this verse.
rows.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو ، وعاصم وابن عامر ( الرياح )

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi reads the plural in twelve locations, adding Ibrahim 14:18 and al-Shura 42:33 to the ten listed places.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع في اثني عشر موضعا هذه العشرة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the plural in five locations: al-Baqara, al-Hijr, al-Kahf, and two places in al-Rum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير : ( الرياح ) في خمسة مواضع

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i reads the plural in three locations: al-Hijr, al-Furqan, and the first al-Rum occurrence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي في ثلاثة مواضع : في الحجر والفرقان والروم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Singular rīḥ can mean the generic wind, so singular and plural readings can convey the same sign; the cited prophetic supplication prefers plural wording for mercy-bearing winds.
rows.anchor: وأما من وحد فإنه يريد به الجنس ، كقولهم : أهلك الناس الدينار والدرهم

rows.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed that a blowing wind be made plural winds rather than a singular wind, associating the plural with mercy.
rows.anchor: ما روي في الحديث من أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا هبت الريح قال : ( اللهم اجعلها رياحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran often uses plural winds for glad tidings of mercy and singular wind for the sterile punishment sent against Ad; Quranic phrasing can mark a specialized sense.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { ومن ءاياته أن يرسل الرياح مبشرات }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He adds that Quranic expressions such as what will make you know about the Hour signal an unspecified matter, unlike expressions that explain what the subject is.
rows.anchor: ما جاء في التنزيل من قوله تعالى : { وما يدريك لعل الساعة قريب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds are named for gliding through air, and their subjugation has three signs: heavy water stays aloft, their measured amount avoids both overcast harm and drought, and God steers them by winds where He wills.
rows.anchor: سمي السحاب سحابا لانسحابه في الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural signs may refer either to all the listed phenomena together or to each phenomenon individually; each of the eight has many indications of a creator.
rows.anchor: لفظ جمع فيحتمل أن يكون ذلك راجعا إلى الكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each sign points to many divine attributes: its coming-to-be indicates power, order indicates knowledge, occurrence at a chosen time indicates will, and coherence without corruption indicates oneness, as 21:22 says.
rows.anchor: ومن حيث أنها وقعت على وجه الاتساق والانتظام من غير ظهور الفساد فيها دلت على وحدانية الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who hold that reason establishes a duty to thank the benefactor, abundant blessings also prove that people owe God sincere gratitude.
rows.anchor: عند من يقول بوجوب شكر المنعم عقلا لأن كثرة النعم توجب الخلوص في الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even indivisible parts of these vast bodies have contingent size, time, and qualities, so every part testifies to dependence on the described creator; all created things thereby praise God in effect.
rows.anchor: كل ما عداه شاهدا على وجوده مقرا بوحدانيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Response means submission and compliance, while faith is a quality of the heart; the servant attains faith's light and strength only after acts of obedience and worship.
rows.anchor: الاستجابة عبارة عن الانقياد والاستسلام

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf reports two readings of yarshudun, with the shīn vowel opened or kasra-marked.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : قرىء { يرشدون } بفتح الشين وكسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who respond and believe are guided to the interests of both religion and worldly life; rashīd describes someone sound in both.
rows.anchor: معنى الآية أنهم إذا استجابوا لي وآمنوا بي : اهتدوا لمصالح دينهم ودنياهم

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Most exegetes say the first Muslim fasting rule barred eating, drinking, and intercourse after sleep or the last evening prayer, and this verse abrogated that rule.
rows.anchor: ذهب جمهور المفسرين إلى أن في أول شريعة محمد

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani says that restriction never belonged to Muslim law; it belonged to the Christians' law, which this verse abrogates, consistent with his denial of abrogation in Islamic law.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم الأصفهاني هذه الحرمة ما كانت ثابتة في شرعنا ألبتة

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority argues that 2:183 compares Muslim fasting to earlier fasting, where the nighttime restriction existed, so the same restriction initially applied to Muslims.
rows.anchor: واحتج الجمهور على قولهم بوجوه . الحجة الأولى : أن قوله تعالى : { كتب عليكم الصيام كما كتب على الذين من قبلكم }

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority argues that saying nighttime intercourse was made lawful would be pointless if it had already been lawful from the start.
rows.anchor: الحجة الثانية : التمسك بقوله تعالى : { أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث إلى نسائكم }

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority reads the believers' self-betrayal as evidence that they had been breaking a prohibition, not doing something already lawful.
rows.anchor: ولو كان ذلك حلالا لهم لما كان بهم حاجة إلى أن يختانون أنفسهم

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority takes God's turning toward and forgiving them to imply that they had sinned by doing what had been prohibited.
rows.anchor: ولولا أن ذلك كان محرما عليهم وأنهم أقدموا على المعصية

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority says the command to be intimate now would have no point if the permission already existed.
rows.anchor: ولو كان الحل ثابتا قبل ذلك كما هو الآن لم يكن لقوله : { فالن باشروهن } فائدة

rows.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: The majority also cites reports about the verse's occasion of revelation as evidence that the restriction had applied in Muslim law.
rows.anchor: الروايات المنقولة في سبب نزول هذه الآية دالة على أن هذه الحرمة كانت ثابتة في شرعنا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim replies that fasting laws need resemble one another only in their basic obligation, not every detail.
rows.anchor: تشبيه الصوم بالصوم يكفي في صدقه مشابهتهما في أصل الوجوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the first majority proof weak: comparison with earlier fasting requires only shared obligation, not identical rules.
rows.anchor: أما الحجة الأولى : فضعيفة لأنا بينا أن تشبيه الصوم بالصوم يكفي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says the permission addresses Muslims by contrast with other communities, for whom the rule remained forbidden.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { أحل لكم } معناه أن الذي كان محرما على غيركم فقد أحل لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the second majority proof weak because the phrase can mean that something forbidden to earlier communities was made lawful for Muslims.
rows.anchor: وأما الحجة الثانية : فضعيفة أيضا لأنا نسلم أن هذه الحرمة كانت ثابتة في شرع من قبلنا

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim says believers inferred that the earlier rule continued because the new fasting command did not expressly remove it, and 2:183's comparison reinforced this suspicion; they therefore abstained and deprived themselves until God clarified the dispensation.
rows.anchor: كان يخطر ببالهم أن تلك الحرمة كانت ثابتة في الشرع المتقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the third proof weak because a plausible but mistaken suspicion of continuity explains their caution; ikhtiyān means depriving themselves of pleasures and interests.
rows.anchor: وأراد به تعالى النظر للمؤمنين بالتخفيف لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root kh-w-n here means deficiency: khāna, ikhtāna, and takhawwana are synonymous forms; believers would have denied themselves nighttime pleasures as Christians did after sleeping.
rows.anchor: وأصل الخيانة النقص ، وخان واختان وتخون بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
rows.claim: Abu Muslim distinguishes human repentance as returning to God in worship from God's repentance as returning to the servant with mercy and beneficence; pardon means overlooking, and the verse describes easing a prior burden.
rows.anchor: التوبة من العباد الرجوع إلى الله تعالى بالعبادة ومن الله الرجوع إلى العبد بالرحمة والإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the fourth majority proof weak: repentance and pardon can describe God's merciful removal of a heavy burden imposed on earlier people, as 7:157 says.
rows.anchor: وأما الحجة الرابعة : فضعيفة لأن التوبة من العباد الرجوع إلى الله تعالى بالعبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the fifth proof weak: believers refrained because of their mistaken suspicion that the earlier restriction continued, then the verse removed that doubt and commanded intimacy.
rows.anchor: فلما بين الله تعالى ذلك وأزال الشبهة فيه لا جرم قال : { فالن باشروهن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sixth proof is weak: a solitary report cannot establish a legally prescribed rule or its abrogation, and the reports' confession detail conflicts with the verse's apparent sense of concealed intercourse.
rows.anchor: قولنا : هذه الآية ناسخة لحكم كان مشروعا لا تعلق له بباب العمل ولا يكون خبر الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reported occasion says a tired Anṣari who had worked all day in the date palms came home after fasting, fell asleep before eating, and awoke unable to eat; Umar also reports having intercourse after the evening prayer, and the verse was revealed after men disclosed what they had done.
rows.anchor: عملت في النخل نهاري أجمع حتى أمسيت فأتيت أهلي لتطعمني شيئا فأبطأت فنمت فأيقظوني

rows.speaker: معاذ
rows.claim: Muadh identifies the tired Anṣari in the occasion report as Abu Sirma.
rows.anchor: فقال معاذ : اسمه أبو صرمة ، وقال البراء : قيس بن صرمة

rows.speaker: البراء
rows.claim: Al-Bara identifies the tired Anṣari as Qays ibn Sirma.
rows.anchor: وقال البراء : قيس بن صرمة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies him as Abu Qays ibn Sirma.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي : أبو قيس بن صرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another version calls him Sirma ibn Anas; the account also says Umar confessed to intercourse after the last evening prayer and the Prophet responded that he had not been worthy of doing so.
rows.anchor: وقيل : صرمة بن أنس ، فسأله رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن سبب ضعفه

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains the reading of uḥilla lakum laylata al-ṣiyām al-rafath as meaning Allah made intimacy lawful.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : قرىء { أحل لكم ليلة الصيام الرفث } أي أحل الله

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Abdullah is reported to read al-rafath as al-rufūth.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله { * الرفوث }

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says the singular phrase night of fasting stands for the plural nights of fasting, a singular used with collective meaning; he introduces a line by Abbas ibn Mirdas as evidence.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : ليلة الصيام أراد ليالي الصيام

rows.speaker: العباس بن مرداس
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi cites Abbas ibn Mirdas's poetry as evidence for using a singular noun where a plural is intended.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول العباس بن مرادس
